Chapter 7—Trusting the Process: Faith and Doubt in Practice.
Every journey, no matter how passionate it begins, eventually hits a few bumps along the way. In Zen, faith isn’t about clinging to some rigid certainty or leaping blindly. Instead, it’s more like a gentle trust—a willingness to keep putting one foot in front of the other, even when you can’t quite see what’s ahead.
And doubt? Well, it’s not the villain we often make it out to be. In fact, doubt has its own place. It can be a loyal companion, nudging you to stay honest, to keep your mind open and curious.
Picture this: Someone’s been practicing for months, maybe even years. One day, those old sparks of excitement are gone. They’re left wondering, “Is this really working? Am I just spinning my wheels?” That dryness—or maybe even boredom—creeps in. It’s so tempting in those moments to just give up, try something new, or start searching for a different teacher.
But here’s the thing—Zen sees these rough patches as a natural part of the path. They’re not mistakes or detours. They’re part of the journey itself.
There’s this story about a practitioner who came to their teacher, confessing all their doubts. The teacher just listened, quietly. And then, simply said, “Just keep sitting.” No big explanations. No magical solutions. Just this gentle reminder: trust the process, even when it feels empty or uncertain.
Most of us expect progress to look like a steady climb up a mountain—always getting better, always feeling more peaceful. But real growth? It’s messy. There are setbacks, plateaus, and days when old habits sneak back in. The heart gets heavy. The mind resists. And yet, it’s in these very moments that faith is shaped—not the faith that’s handed down, but the kind you earn by sticking with it, day after day.
Here’s something to pay attention to: Doubt, when you meet it with curiosity instead of fear, can actually open new doors. It keeps your mind flexible, ready to question what you think you know, and explore unfamiliar ground. The trick is not to let yourself get stuck—let doubt pass through, just like a cloud drifting by.
Over time, something shifts. A quiet confidence starts to grow—not because you have all the answers, but because you’ve weathered a few storms and you’re still here. The practice becomes less about chasing some special state, and more about simply being present for whatever shows up, trusting that each moment has its own kind of wisdom.
In the end, faith and doubt walk together. Each plays a role in how your understanding unfolds. The journey keeps going—not because you’re certain of the outcome, but because you’re willing to keep showing up, day after day, meeting life just as it is.
